What the badges mean

Performance

● Noisy
Fired often over the weeks shown, and few of its firings caught something; with weeks, how many weeks running.
⚠︎ Caught nothing
Fired a few times, under the noisy bar, and none of the firings judged caught an incident: not noisy yet, and not OK.
? No record
Fired often over the weeks shown, with no incident written down to judge it by: whether its firings mattered isn't known.
○ OK
Fired over the weeks shown, and isn't noisy.
– Silent
No firing in the weeks shown.
⧉ Spare
Another rule caught every incident it caught, as soon, at the same severity or above.

Trust

≠ Differs
Over the last week checked, its replay differed from what really fired.
◌ Not replayed
Lapilli can't replay it; its page says why.
⇣ Recorded only
Copied in from where it fired: what it fired is known, not its condition.

Disposition

✓ keep
Its note says to keep it as it is.
± tune
Its note says to tune it.
⊘ retire
Its note says to retire it.

Progress

✎ Proposed
A change to it is proposed and not finished with.
⚠︎ Problems to check
What it says when it fires has problems of fact; the badge, “n to check”, counts them with whatever else its page lists to check.

Expectations

✕ Broken
An expectation it is held to is broken: a budget in the week so far or the last whole week, a catch, or a scenario.

In order of: caught nothing, the most first re-fired, the most first

? 1 of the 4 weeks shown had no incident written down for them or the two weeks before: their firings are counted, not judged. Write incidents down

Why

A firing is judged by the incidents written down in its week and the two weeks before. With none, a firing that caught nothing can't be told from one nobody wrote down.
